text:
Connor Bedard put it plainly to The Athletic's Mark Lazerus: "WE all said we think we're going to win this year. WE set the expectations on ourselves." Seventeen games in, the Blackhawks are 4-12-1, with a playoff chance that rounds to zero.

It isn't bad luck. They are winless in five, outscored 23-11, with 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) in that stretch and 42.23% for the season. Arvid Soderblom has made it worse, .846 and 4.7 goals below expected over his last four starts. The Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pair has been caught out most, 34% of the expected goals and a 4-10 goal hole.

Scott Powers and Lazerus listed eight changes Kyle Davidson should consider at The Athletic, and the pressure on the front office is now a fair topic.

There is one thing to like. Lazerus called Roman Kantserov a coming star, and the line he plays on with Bedard and Patrick Kane is worth your attention even while it gets outshot. For this season, the honest goal is growth in those minutes.
headline: Bedard raised the bar, the Hawks haven't
